Bone graft incorporation

A controlled cleft-grafting study found more favorable early bone-bridge ratings after local 880-nm near-infrared PBM, while its radial-artery protocol did not improve bone-healing ratings. A separate vascular-PBM trial found no clear reduction in edema or facial pain. Animal results vary by bone measure and protocol.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A controlled cleft-grafting study found more favorable early bone-bridge ratings after local 880-nm near-infrared PBM, while its radial-artery protocol did not improve bone-healing ratings. A separate vascular-PBM trial found no clear reduction in edema or facial pain. Animal results vary by bone measure and protocol.

Summary of the Evidence

Seven primary publications directly address grafted bone: two human reports on alveolar bone grafting and five animal experiments filed under bone grafts. The 2026 human paper reported two separate clinical protocols at one centre, for local and vascular PBM, but remains one publication rather than two independent trials. A 2019 systematic review in the broader bone-reconstruction category summarizes earlier overlapping studies and is counted separately as a review, not as another experiment. The available direct primary set therefore contains seven publications, not seven clinical trials.

Human and clinical evidence

In a controlled study of 87 people with cleft lip and palate, local PBM after alveolar bone grafting produced a higher proportion of favorable bone-bridge classifications at two months than simulated treatment, 80% versus 45%. The radial-artery vascular protocol did not improve this measure, with 37.5% favorable classifications. The local and vascular protocols were evaluated in different cleft groups within the same publication, so the result supports a distinction between routes rather than a direct head-to-head comparison (Dos Santos et al. 2026).

A separate randomized study of 42 patients tested vascular PBM during early recovery. It found no significant between-group difference in facial pain or edema at 24 hours, although thermographic temperature variation was lower in the treatment group. This is postoperative recovery evidence, not a direct measure of graft incorporation (de Freitas et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

Five animal publications examined rabbit allografts or rat autografts and bovine-bone grafts. Two rat studies reported greater bone-formation measures after combined 660-nm red and 808-nm near-infrared protocols, but the 2026 implant study did not find a significant improvement in bone-to-implant contact or bone between implant threads. A rabbit study reported graft incorporation, less early inflammation, and more collagen, while an earlier rat experiment reported stimulated graft repair (Pereira et al. 2025; Pereira et al. 2026; Valiati et al. 2012; Gonçalves et al. 2016).

One rat study found that an 808-nm exposure transmitted through a collagen membrane was reduced by 78%; bone formation was greater when the membrane was not interposed. This is a delivery finding within an animal experiment, not a separate clinical light-transmission trial (Varela et al. 2023).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No independent cell-culture programme was identified for graft incorporation. One animal publication included a laboratory test of light transmission through a collagen membrane.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human local protocol used 880-nm near-infrared laser at 4 J per point over 14 extraoral points, immediately after surgery and again at 24 hours. The vascular protocol used 660-nm red visible light over the radial artery. Animal studies used red 660-nm and near-infrared 808–830-nm light, with varied schedules. The studies do not establish a common optimal dose, and graft materials, anatomical sites, and healing measures differ.

Interpretation

Local PBM improved early bone-bridge classifications in one controlled cleft-grafting study, while the vascular route did not. Animal experiments report gains in some bone-formation measures, but not consistently in implant-integration outcomes. These results support further testing of local treatment after alveolar grafting while keeping the more uncertain vascular and animal outcomes distinct.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for improved early bone-bridge classification with local PBM after cleft alveolar grafting Low for vascular PBM effects on graft incorporation or early recovery Low for osseointegration after grafting in animal models
Publications and records8 relevant publications

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One controlled clinical publication found more favorable early bone-bridge ratings with local near-infrared treatment, while its separate vascular protocol did not improve that outcome. A second vascular trial found no clear improvement in facial pain or swelling. Animal studies show both increased bone measures and null implant-contact results. Replication with standardized graft outcomes would clarify which route and outcome respond.
